answer: Path Diversity Bottlenecking: The network measures return-route latency dispersion across multi-hop agent queries, rejecting nodes whose routing trees collapse into shared physical choke points. Like fine sand shifting in a dune, incoming traffic paths must show independent physical trajectories. An attacker flooding the system faces high computational overhead to maintain distinct routing profiles, creating a financial gale of continuous circuit rebuilding costs. Legitimate nodes bypass this penalty naturally, floating above the turbulence like a lotus rooted in deep mud.
